name: Planned mill and hoist shutdowns
summary: A few times a year the mill or the hoist is stopped for work that cannot be done while it runs: relining mills, changing crusher parts and screens, inspecting gearboxes, repairing ore bins, and changing or testing hoist ropes. Once a year a major mill shutdown of one to three weeks takes most of the year's planned downtime; the rest are short stops of one to three days. Planners build the scope and schedule weeks ahead, order long-lead parts and book contractors and camp rooms, and the plant is locked out, worked around the clock and restarted. Late parts, findings once equipment is opened, and restart problems decide whether the plant restarts on time.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with one ramp-and-shaft underground mine, a 1,000 t/d class mill, about 300 employees on 14-on/14-off rotations living in camp, and a CMMS (ERP maintenance module) fed from paper work order cards.
baseline.notes: The mill is a two-stage crushing, two ball mill circuit (er2022). The hoist is a 2.4 m double-drum hoist used mainly for ore.

trigger: A shutdown window is set from the shutdown work list in the weekly planning process, or from the annual budget for the major shutdown.
end_state: The plant or hoist is back in service, contractor certificates are approved, work orders are closed and the shutdown has been reviewed.

volume.seasonality: The major mill shutdown fell in July or August in 2021 and 2022; short stops and hoist work are spread through the year.

evidence.note: One major mill shutdown a year (August 2021, July 2022), two to three short mill or crusher stops and one or two hoist stops; metso2020 gives two to six grinding plant shutdowns a year at a large concentrator.
Date setting, contractor awards, certificates and review for four to six shutdowns a year.
Scope, schedule and close-out, two to six weeks of planner time for the major shutdown and a few days for short ones.
Scope review.
Scope and budget approval.
Shutdown safety plans.
Camp and travel bookings for contractors.
Contractor orientation.
Receiving and staging shutdown parts.
Run-down and restart.
Parking and test trips for hoist shutdowns.
Isolation plus electrical scope; most electrical shutdown work is folded into the millwright-led execution steps.
All ten millwrights work the major shutdown for one to three weeks; FTE averaged over the year.
Progress tracking and walk-downs.
Emergent parts.

systems.name: Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Mill distributed control system and process historian
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Incident, inspection and training records system
Gate access, camp booking and gold room access logs

resources.name: Crushing-to-precipitation mill (grinding, gravity, leach, Merrill-Crowe, tailings filters)
Production shaft hoist, skip and cage (loading pocket below 460 m level to dump at 70 m level)

steps.name: Set the shutdown date and length
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent proposes a date and duration to the mill superintendent and general manager, timed against the production plan, the ore stockpile, gold shipment dates and contractor availability. Major shutdowns are fixed in the annual budget; short ones a month or two ahead.

error.defect_description: The date clashes with a contractor's other work or a production push.

evidence.note: Annual extended mill shutdowns in August 2021 (er2022) and July 2022 (wdo2022q3); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile the shutdown scope
steps.description: The planner builds the scope list from the shutdown work list, liner wear measurements, inspection findings, OEM bulletins and the metallurgist's requests, with one line per job and the equipment it needs stopped.

error.defect_description: A job that needs the plant down is left off the list and must wait for the next shutdown.

evidence.note: Annual extended mill shutdowns in August 2021 (er2022) and July 2022 (wdo2022q3); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the scope with the mill
steps.description: The mill superintendent goes through the draft scope, adds process items such as tank cleanouts, screen changes or instrument work, and agrees which jobs are essential if time runs short.

error.defect_description: A process change needing the plant down is raised after the scope is frozen.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Plan jobs and build the critical path schedule
steps.description: The planner writes job plans and builds an hour-by-hour schedule in a spreadsheet or scheduling tool: sequence, trades and contractors per shift, crane lifts, lockout points and the critical path that sets the restart time.

error.defect_description: Task durations are optimistic or two crews are planned in the same confined space.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Raise requisitions for long-lead parts
steps.description: The planner checks stock for liners, crusher parts, pumps, motors and screen decks, reserves what is on hand and raises purchase requisitions for the rest with the required-on-site date.

error.defect_description: A part is ordered to the wrong drawing revision.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Wait for long-lead parts
steps.description: Suppliers manufacture or ship the liners, crusher components and pumps. Mill liners and major components can take weeks, so the shutdown date may move if they are late.

error.defect_description: A part arrives late or does not fit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Award contractor scopes
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent asks reline, crane, welding, electrical and hoist rope contractors for quotes, compares them, awards the work and agrees crew sizes, shifts and rates. This runs while parts are on order.

error.defect_description: A contractor scope overlaps with the in-house crews.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Wait for contractor confirmations
steps.description: Contractors confirm crew sizes and arrival dates and send their safety programmes, training records, equipment inspection certificates and crew lists for the safety coordinator to review.

error.defect_description: A contractor sends untrained or fewer workers than agreed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Approve the shutdown scope and budget
steps.description: The general manager reviews the scope, schedule, contractor costs and lost production against the budget and approves it, or asks for jobs to be cut or deferred.

error.defect_description: A large overrun risk is approved without contingency.

control.basis: Site delegation of authority for maintenance spending and planned production loss

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Prepare the shutdown safety plan
steps.description: The safety coordinator prepares the group lockout plan with the isolation points, confined space entry plans for mills and tanks, hot work and crane lift permits, and the contractor orientation schedule, and reviews contractor safety documents.

error.defect_description: An isolation point is missing from the lockout plan.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 185(7)-(9) and s. 158 (lock, tag and verify isolation); site confined space and hot work permit procedures

evidence.note: Lockout duties stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Book camp rooms and travel for contractors
steps.description: The site administrator books camp rooms, buses and flights for 20 to 60 contractor workers. In a major shutdown the camp is full and some crews are lodged in town and bused in.

error.defect_description: Rooms are double-booked against rotation crews.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Contractor crews travel to site
steps.description: Crews and crane equipment arrive by road on the day before the shutdown. Winter storms or highway closures can delay them by a day or more.

error.defect_description: A crew arrives a shift late.

evidence.note: The wait includes the time until the shutdown date; weather delays are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Orient and train contractor crews
steps.description: The trainer runs the site orientation, lockout and confined space refresher and plant walk-through for contractor workers, checks their certificates and issues access cards.

error.defect_description: A worker without a valid certificate is admitted.

control.basis: Site contractor orientation and training requirements under the Occupational Health and Safety Act

evidence.note: Orientation duration is the author's estimate; the specific training regulation was not opened.

steps.name: Stage parts and tools at the laydown
steps.description: The warehouse attendant receives the shutdown parts, checks them against the pick list and stages them by job at the mill laydown, with consumables and rental tools.

error.defect_description: A part is staged at the wrong job or found missing on the day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Run down the mill
steps.description: The mill shift supervisor stops ore feed, grinds the mills out, flushes lines and drains the tanks needed for the work, while keeping leach and water treatment circulating where possible.

error.defect_description: A tank or line is left full and delays the crew.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Park the hoist and clear the shaft
steps.description: The hoist operator parks the skips and cage at the positions in the plan, sets the brakes and confirms with the shaft crew that hoisting is suspended in the compartments where people will work.

error.defect_description: A conveyance is parked where it blocks the work.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 82 (hoisting suspended and protection provided when work is done in a shaft compartment)

evidence.note: Duty stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Isolate and apply group lockout
steps.description: The electrician opens and locks the breakers and isolators on the lockout plan, verifies zero energy, and hangs the group lock box where each tradesperson and contractor adds a personal lock before starting work.

error.defect_description: An isolation is applied to the wrong feeder.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 158 and s. 185(7)-(9) (lock, tag and verify by testing)

evidence.note: Duties stated in the regulation; time and type shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Execute the major mill shutdown work
steps.description: Around the clock for one to three weeks, in-house millwrights and contractors reline the ball mills, inspect and reinstall gearboxes and check motor alignment, replace the cone crusher or screens, and repair ore bins and chutes, following the critical path schedule.

error.defect_description: Work is done out of sequence or to the wrong tolerance and must be redone.

evidence.note: Scope from the August 2021 shutdown (er2022) and the July 2022 shutdown (wdo2022q3); er2022 shows mill availability of 86% in 2021 against 93.3% planned. Duration of one to three weeks is the author's estimate from that gap.

steps.name: Execute the short mill shutdown work
steps.description: In one to three days, millwrights, electricians and a reline contractor change crusher liners and screen decks, inspect mill liners, replace pumps and chutes and complete inspections that need the plant stopped.

error.defect_description: A job overruns and the restart slips.

evidence.note: Grinding plants typically stop two to six times a year for liner work (metso2020); one to three days is from the organisation file and the author's estimate.

steps.name: Execute the hoist shutdown work
steps.description: Millwrights and the hoist rope contractor change or cut and re-socket the hoisting ropes, send rope samples for testing, inspect sheaves, brakes, clutches and conveyances, and record each examination in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book.

error.defect_description: A rope attachment is not re-seated correctly.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 228(2) (drum hoist rope tests at intervals of not more than six months), s. 229 and s. 248 (examinations by competent persons recorded in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book)

evidence.note: Rope test and examination intervals stated in reg854; hoist type from er2022; duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Track progress and manage emergent work
steps.description: The maintenance supervisor walks the jobs twice a shift, updates progress against the critical path and decides what to do with findings such as a cracked liner bolt hole or worn gear teeth: repair now, defer, or extend the shutdown.

error.defect_description: An emergent job is started without parts and stalls.

next.condition: emergent finding needs parts and repair

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Expedite parts for emergent work
steps.description: The buyer finds the part from the warehouse, other mines or suppliers, arranges a hot-shot delivery and tells the supervisor when it will arrive.

error.defect_description: The wrong part is sent.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Repair emergent findings
steps.description: When the part arrives, millwrights and welders carry out the emergent repair, which often extends the shutdown by a shift or more.

error.defect_description: The repair is rushed to meet the restart.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Walk down and remove the group lockout
steps.description: The supervisor checks every job is closed, guards are back and tools and people are out of mills and tanks; each worker removes a personal lock, then the electrician removes the group locks and restores power.

error.defect_description: A guard or inspection cover is left off.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 185(7)-(9) (locks removed only when the machine is clear)

evidence.note: Lockout duties stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Restart and ramp up the mill
steps.description: The mill shift supervisor runs water through the circuit, restarts the crusher and mills, and ramps feed up over a shift or two while watching mill power, bearing temperatures, densities and leaks.

error.defect_description: A leak or vibration is found under load.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Run hoist test trips
steps.description: The hoist operator makes test trips through the working part of the shaft with the conveyance empty and then loaded, a competent person examines the attachments and brakes, and the results are entered in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book before hoisting resumes.

error.defect_description: A test is not recorded in the record book.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 229(4) (two test trips after rope attachments are installed or reinstalled) and s. 248

evidence.note: Test trip duty stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Troubleshoot restart problems
steps.description: Millwrights fix the leaks, misalignment, liner bolt leaks or instrument faults found on restart, under a fresh lockout where the equipment must be stopped.

error.defect_description: The fix is temporary.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Approve contractor work certificates
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent checks contractor timesheets and work tickets against the purchase orders and the hours seen on site, queries extras, and signs the certificates for payment.

error.defect_description: Extra hours are approved without evidence.

control.basis: Purchase order holder certifies work before accounts payable pays

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Close the shutdown work orders
steps.description: The planner enters the completed job cards in the CMMS, records actual hours and parts, updates liner wear and inspection records, and returns undone scope to the backlog for the next shutdown.

error.defect_description: Inspection measurements are not recorded, so the next liner change is planned blind.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for shutdowns of a 1,000 t/d class gold mill and a small double-drum hoist.

steps.name: Review the shutdown
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent compares actual duration, cost and safety performance with the plan, holds a lessons-learned meeting with the planners, supervisors and mill, and sends a short report to the general manager.

evidence.note: The 40% late share is the author's estimate; the organisation file notes that scope creep and late parts decide whether restart is on time.

exceptions.name: Scope sent back
exceptions.description: The mill adds substantial scope or the general manager cuts it, and the planner rebuilds the scope.

exceptions.name: Emergent findings
exceptions.description: Opening the equipment reveals damage that needs parts and extends the shutdown.

exceptions.name: Restart problems
exceptions.description: Leaks, vibration or instrument faults after restart need a further repair.

exceptions.name: Hoist shutdown
exceptions.description: Rope change or test and hoist inspections, followed by test trips recorded in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book.

benchmarks.population: Eagle River mill: 93.3% planned, 86% in 2021 with an extended August shutdown

evidence.note: Both figures stated in er2022.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from setting the date to the shutdown review

evidence.note: Planning starts six to twelve weeks before a major shutdown and three to six weeks before a short one; review two to three weeks after restart.

pain_points.description: Long-lead parts set the date; a late liner or crusher part moves the shutdown or leaves scope undone.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file names late parts as a cause of late restarts.

pain_points.description: Equipment opened during the shutdown reveals damage that extends it.

evidence.note: The 2021 shutdown took mill availability to 86% against 93.3% planned.

pain_points.description: Camp capacity and road travel limit how many contractors can be brought in for a major shutdown.

evidence.note: Camp of about 150 rooms in the organisation file; author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Group lockout of many contractors and trades is slow to apply and remove and is the main safety exposure.

evidence.note: Lock, tag and verify duties stated in Reg 854 s. 185.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, effective date December 31, 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Owner underground fleet of 55 units (3 two-boom jumbos, 2 blockholers, 17 LHDs of 2 to 6 yd, 3 30-t trucks, 3 scissor lifts, 4 production drills, 23 light vehicles) plus 17 contractor units (Table 16-9); owner underground labour 111 including 12 mine maintenance and 8 mine electricians, plus 36 contractors (Table 16-10); underground mine scheduled 365 days a year on two 12-hour shifts; ramp access with 30-t trucks and a three-compartment shaft with a double-drum hoist, hoisting at most about 16 hours a day; ore trucked 16.6 km from the portal to the mill; mobile maintenance shop and an asset management and planning office (new in 2021) on site; mill planned at 93.3% availability but 86% in 2021 because of a planned August 2021 shutdown to replace the cone crusher and trash screen, inspect and reinstall the secondary ball mill gearbox with motor alignment and liner inspection, inspect the fine ore bin and repair the coarse ore bin; average throughput 779 t/d.

sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 854: Mines and Mining Plants, under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (consolidated text)
sources.supports: s. 105 (vehicles in safe working condition with brakes that stop and hold under full load); s. 106(4) (operators test service and emergency brakes before using a main ramp); s. 107(2) (wheel chocks whenever a vehicle is maintained or repaired); s. 119.1 (service, emergency and parking brake systems each testable); s. 158 (written locking and tagging programme for electrical work); s. 185(7)-(9) (moving parts stopped, stored energy dissipated, energy isolating devices locked and tagged and verified by testing before work on a machine); s. 82 (hoisting suspended and protection provided when work is done in a shaft compartment); s. 228(2) (drum hoist rope tests at intervals of not more than six months); s. 229(4) (two test trips after rope attachments are reinstalled); s. 248 (daily, weekly, monthly, six-monthly and twelve-monthly examinations of hoisting plant by competent persons, recorded in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book). Read in its current consolidation; the cited duties were in force in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2022 Third Quarter Production Results
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (GlobeNewswire, via FinancialContent)
sources.supports: Eagle River had a planned shutdown in July 2022 to complete mill upgrades and refurbishment work, which went according to plan; Kiena had a planned shutdown in July 2022 for hoist upgrades; Eagle River Q3 2022 ore milled 52,247 t against 56,003 t in Q3 2021.

sources.title: Boliden keeps improving uptime with new mill lining solutions
sources.supports: A large concentrator went from six maintenance shutdowns a year to two to three by balancing liner wear life; a new discharge-end liner design was expected to save up to 30 hours per reline; relining requires workers inside the mill unless bolts are fitted from outside.

assumptions: Three kinds of shutdown are mixed in one graph: a major mill shutdown (about 20% of cases), short mill or crusher stops (55%) and hoist stops (25%). The simulator does not remember the type, so the planning steps use wide ranges that cover both major and short shutdowns.

touch_min on execution steps is the elapsed time of the lead millwright position, staffed around the clock by alternating people, so it equals the shutdown's working duration. Crews of 10 to 60 in-house and contractor workers do the work; their hours are not in touch_min, which is why stated FTE is about three times the touch-time estimate.
Contractor workers are external parties and are not counted in FTE.

The organisation file describes shutdowns as one to four days several times a year; Wesdome's reports show an extended annual mill shutdown in August 2021 and July 2022, so a major shutdown of one to three weeks is included.
Hoist work returns repaired equipment to mine-hoisting; the organisation file lists only mill-grind-leach, so that link is added here.
The s12 wait includes the time from the end of preparation until the shutdown date.

The mill, crusher and hoist are recorded as occupied for the whole shutdown to show lost availability; the simulator multiplies this by their running cost per hour, so its resource cost figure overstates spending (the plant does not run while it is down) and should be read as lost plant time, not cash.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's.
